Working principles

Frame preciselyClarify objective, constraints, customers and success criteria.
Make the decisionCompare options and trade-offs; choose a path rather than hiding behind ambiguity.
Measure by sliceGlobal averages do not replace locale, model, device and version-level quality.
Protect critical gatesPrivacy, safety, reliability and severe customer-quality failures remain explicit constraints.
Design for failureObservability, retries, fallbacks, rollback and human review are part of the architecture.
Make learning reusableConvert recurring failures into tooling, validation, platform or operating mechanisms.

Internationalization

Translation changes words. Localization changes experience. i18n makes it scalable.

ConceptWhat it solvesWhat can failHow to test
UnicodeUniversal encoding model for scripts/charactersNormalization, grapheme length, emoji, mixed scriptsCanonical-equivalence, grapheme, script-mixing cases
ICU / CLDRLocale-aware formatting/data rulesPlural, date, currency, collation, display-name errorsLocale matrix + golden expected outputs
XLIFF / String CatalogsStructured localization workflow/resourcesMissing/stale strings, context loss, placeholder corruptionBuild-time checks, extraction, localization completeness
RTL / bidiCorrect directionality/layoutBroken mixed text, punctuation/numbers, UI mirroringArabic/Hebrew + mixed Latin/numeric cases
Plural / genderGrammatical agreementWrong forms despite semantically correct outputLocale-specific quantity/person cases
Code switchingReal multilingual utterancesRouting, language mixing, guardrail gapsMixed-language prompts and unsupported fragments
TransliterationCross-script renderingNames/places distortedNamed-entity gold sets by language/script
Locale fallbackGraceful behavior when exact locale unavailableWrong language/region defaultUnsupported locale + fallback-chain tests
Multilingual ML evaluation

The unit of quality is a slice, not a global average.

Feature × Locale × Model × Device × OS Version

Version the dataset and evaluator too. Model updates and OS changes can shift behavior even when feature code is unchanged.

Evaluation stack

1 · Data

Native-authored / native-reviewed golden sets, long-tail slices, code switching, safety, cultural cases, low-resource coverage.

2 · Automated eval

Task success, deterministic correctness, semantic similarity, safety, latency, regression detection, calibrated LLM judge.

3 · Human eval

Native fluency, register, culture, naturalness. Use sampling/adjudication to control cost.

4 · Slice analysis

Locale + intent + device + model + OS + severity. Add confidence intervals/sample-size checks.

5 · Triage

Classify data vs model vs prompt vs feature vs evaluator vs infrastructure problem.

6 · Launch gate

GO / HOLD / ROLLBACK per locale based on primary metrics + guardrails + critical failure count.

International intelligence quality framework

Correct — meaning/task success. Natural — native fluency/register. Relevant — locale/cultural context. Safe — locale-specific safety and unsupported-language behavior. Reliable — regressions/consistency across model/device/OS. Performant — latency/resource budget. Private — data-handling constraints. “I would not average these into one number if a critical guardrail can fail.”

First 90 days

Learn before prescribing.

0–30 · Baseline

  • Map feature/model/language/QE/PM ownership.
  • Understand current eval + locale gate mechanisms.
  • Baseline top regressions/tooling bottlenecks.
  • Learn team-specific Apple platform workflows.

31–60 · Pilot

  • Propose shared error taxonomy / readiness scorecard.
  • Pilot one high-friction eval/tooling improvement.
  • Identify reusable datasets/evals across features.

61–90 · Scale

  • Drive first measurable international milestone.
  • Operationalize regression triage / launch gate.
  • Publish shared practices and investment roadmap.
